metadata.title: Nonunique nearest stable complex quadratics
metadata.description:
For every fixed positive-definite real coefficient inner product, unstable complex quadratics with at least two distinct attained global nearest closed-left-half-plane stable quadratics occur arbitrarily close to z^2, both in monic coefficient space and in the full exact-degree coefficient space. A limiting normal has cubic support against a quartic squared displacement, disproving stable-set prox-regularity; compact localization ensures full-degree global attainment. The same obstruction disproves set prox-regularity of the whole abscissa epigraph. The monic quadratic abscissa nevertheless is function prox-regular at the origin relative to each finite limiting subgradient, with constants depending on that subgradient in the real Euclidean coefficient metric.

This gives a negative answer in degree two to Lewis's historical question about the stable complex monic set. The later Oberwolfach Question1 omits the coefficient field, normalization and metric; its complex convention is explicitly qualified. The note credits Bottema and Kirillov-Overton classical stability-boundary geometry, Burke-Overton/Lewis first-order root analysis, the Poliquin-Rockafellar-Thibault projection characterization, and earlier nearest-polynomial approximation work of Moses-Liu and Orban de Xivry. No real-only or all-degree classification, explicit unstable input and minimizing pair, general nonlinear parameter-metric transfer, firstness or present-day openness guarantee is claimed. The limiting support covector is horizontal; the representing normal vector need not be horizontal in mixed coefficient-height metrics.

metadata.title: Missing faces and topological embeddings of sphere skeleta
metadata.description:
Let S be a finite simplicial triangulation of the topological sphere S^(2d), and let T be a missing d-face. We prove that adjoining T to the d-skeleton of S prevents a topological embedding in S^(2d). For d >= 3, a graded Koszul calculation combines with established ambient-completion, anisotropy and metastable embedding theorems. For d = 2, we apply the Nevo-Wagner bistellar transfer theorem in the PL class supplied by the given triangulation: a contractible complementary manifold supplies the required disk map, and a flag subdivision supplies the base. This proves the statement of their Conjecture 1.3 without a standard PL structure assumption on the source. No claim of first priority or a new general method is made.

metadata.title: No single polynomial inequality defines a real binary Gram locus
metadata.description:
For a real tensor with n binary factors, the Gram locus is the tuple of determinants of its one-mode Gram matrices as the tensor ranges over the closed Frobenius unit ball. For every n>=3, no single real polynomial nonnegativity condition in those determinant coordinates defines this locus inside the cube [0,1/4]^n, or inside its known convex hull. This gives a negative answer to Seigal's single-polynomial question for n>=4. The self-contained proof uses established marginal polygon inequalities, an explicit real three-factor realization, exact polynomial multiplicities and zero-determinant slices. A strictly positive rational four-factor tuple also passes the proposed polynomial condition but is unrealizable at any allowed norm.

The marginal criteria and real constructions of Higuchi-Sudbery-Szulc, Bravyi and Domanov-Stegeman-De Lathauwer are credited antecedents. Sinn's earlier general boundary/interior obstruction is also credited. Alper Ferudun's unrefereed October 2, 2026 preprint, DOI10.5281/zenodo.23111048, contains an overlapping stronger theorem, including an all-positive domain. Our original theorem-bearing proof is present in GitHub PR170, created September 30, 2026 at13:15:23UTC, and is unchanged. We describe these as contemporaneous separate disclosures. metadata.title: Local Ricci-pinching maxima on an almost-abelian group
metadata.description:
Lauret's July 2018 talk announced nonglobal local maxima of the Ricci pinching functional that are not solvsolitons of the specified transitive group. This research note gives a self-contained small-parameter proof for the known Lauret-Will family A_u = J direct-sum uE_12. For each u strictly between zero and one half, its standard metric is a non-strict local maximum of Scal^2/||Ric||^2, with value 1/3, among all nearby left-invariant metrics on the fixed five-dimensional simply connected solvable group. It fails that group's equation Ric = cI + D for a derivation D, and a same-group metric has value 9/17.

This gives an explicit negative answer to the literal fixed-group assertion in Morgan-Pansu Question 14. The proof covers the full space of nearby metrics through an orthogonal slice with an unrestricted cross-block and a uniform remainder estimate along a constant-value family. The metric is nevertheless a geometric Ricci soliton, isometric to the product of the Euclidean plane and the three-dimensional Heisenberg group. The earlier exact existence announcement and known family/value are credited. No novelty, first assertion, first proof, or present community-open status is claimed. metadata.title: An elementary counterexample to a Nullstellensatz for finite-type link invariants
metadata.description:
We give a principal-ideal counterexample to the arbitrary-ideal actual-link Nullstellensatz in the ordinary uncompleted complex algebra of all finite-order finite-type link invariants. With g the sum of squared pairwise linking numbers and f=g(4g-1), the nonempty common zero set is the algebraically split links, but g does not lie in the radical of fV. A character on the entire algebra is obtained by formal evaluation of the standard twist-restriction polynomial at one half. The result applies for every fixed component count m at least two and for all finite-component links; the source's separate indexed linking-number ideal in the labelled theory is not decided.

This is an elementary application of older polynomiality, explicitly credited to Stanford-Trapp, Eisermann and Stoimenow. metadata.title: Positive tangent-bundle Seshadri constants characterize projective space
metadata.description:
Let X be a smooth integral projective variety of dimension n at least one over an algebraically closed field of arbitrary characteristic. Positivity of the relative Fulger-Murayama Seshadri constant of the tangent bundle at one arbitrary closed point implies that X is projective n-space. The five-page research note proves Fulger-Murayama Conjecture 4.9 without assuming Fano, global tangent nefness, characteristic zero, or a general point.

An absolute minimum of ample degree through the specified point eliminates the boundary of the one-marked stable-map family. Very-free evaluation and the actual contracted marking section give numerical Picard rank one and ampleness of the anticanonical divisor; the established Fano clause completes the proof. Standard numerical-generation methods, Mori/Kollar, Fulger-Murayama, and Chang's toric case are credited. The source and verification archive preserves the frozen original candidate, independent mathematical reviews, a documented 64-query priority audit, and portable integrity and finite controls. Those computations do not formally verify the geometric theorem.

metadata.title: A Robinson counterexample to ideal-only tangency certificates
metadata.description:
The classical Robinson sextic is globally nonnegative, but adding any nonnegative constant does not make it a finite sum of real polynomial squares modulo even the full ideal of polynomials vanishing on its real tangency variety. This refutes both the exact ordinary-radical certificate and the every-positive-epsilon original-ideal certificate proposed in the unrestricted tangency-minor formulation of Schweighofer's 2007 question. metadata.title: A smooth Reshetnyak-harmonic sphere with unbounded distortion
metadata.description:

metadata.title: Finite-energy lattice percolation with internal critical probability one
metadata.description:
For every integer d at least 2, we construct a nearest-neighbor bond percolation on the integer lattice Z^d whose law is invariant under every graph automorphism and mixing under translations. It has ordinary finite energy: both single-edge conditional states have strictly positive probability given all the other output edges. Almost surely there is a unique infinite component C, but the quenched internal Bernoulli bond and site critical probabilities of X and C equal one. Every independent thinning with retention p below one destroys all infinite components. This gives an affirmative construction for the historical ordinary-energy question of Benjamini, Haggstrom and Schramm, restated in Benjamini's Saint-Flour notes and by Benjamini and Tassion.

The construction develops Haggstrom-Mester's published one-ended-tree summable-flip mechanism. Tree edges are deleted with probability 2^(-s), where s is their finite-side size; a non-tree edge is inserted with probability 2^(-M), where M is the maximum finite-side size along its connecting tree path. This dimension independent rule suppresses every bypass and leaves eventually singleton cut boundaries along each ray. Timar's established equivariant one-ended spanning-tree theorem supplies the all-dimensional input. The note also proves a planar bounded-cutset consequence of the exact fixed-phase midpoint projection of the older Haggstrom-Mester site model, whose unchanged flip rates are 4^(-s). That consequence is a deduction supplied here, not a theorem located in the inspected older paper. No wholly new planar perturbation mechanism, verified first resolution, certified novelty of the all-dimensional rule, or worldwide current-open-status claim is made. No uniform energy bound or failure of every uniform marginal bound is asserted.

metadata.title: Property (T) above one-third density in random free-product quotients
metadata.description:
Fix at least three nontrivial finitely generated groups, a finite nonempty inverse-closed generating alphabet of nonidentity elements in each factor, and a density 1/3 less than d less than 1. For the quotient by floor(|S_l|^d) independent uniform rooted cyclically reduced syllable relators of exact length l, sampled with replacement, the probability of Kazhdan property (T) tends to one through all integer lengths. This gives an affirmative resolution of the at-least-three-factor property-(T) question in Problem 16 of the 2026 Oberwolfach report Median Geometry and Applications. Fixed-radius word-ball alphabets with integer radius at least one are included. The theorem does not settle the broader two-factor Question 1.9 of Random Quotients of Free Products, the critical density 1/3, or varying-parameter uniformity. Known collapse already gives property (T) above 1/2; the substantive extension includes every density in (1/3,1/2].

The present argument supplies the exact weighted endpoint kernel, torsion-compatible inverse-fixed-block deletion and suffix choices, unequal-length type-matrix spectrum, and concentration of independent whole-relator Laplacians. It uses established Ballmann-Swiatkowski-Zuk/Kotowski-Kotowski and Tropp results. metadata.title: Deep derived pure braids need not be 1-solvable
metadata.description:

metadata.title: A vertex maximum principle for subcritical reinforcement
metadata.description:

metadata.title: A classical Wu-manifold answer to a free-rank question
metadata.description:
The fixed Wu manifold W = SU(3)/SO(3), with the real-matrix SO(3) inclusion, is a finite simply connected complex of rational homotopy type S^5. Its actual continuous free toral rank and free 2-rank are zero, while its free p-rank is one for every odd prime p. Every cyclic group of odd order acts freely and smoothly on this same W. This supplies an affirmative answer to the existence question printed on page 1912 of Hanke's OWR 32/2010 contribution, under its literal actual-space free-action definitions and all its homotopy hypotheses. Almost-free and rational toral ranks are different invariants; no replacement space or prime-dependent space is used.

This explanatory research note assembles classical facts. Yeroshkin's 2014 preprint and 2015 circle-isotropy calculation already contain the weights (1,1,-2), whose odd cyclic subgroups act freely. Kuhn and Lloyd's 2020 preprint already explicitly discusses the no-free-Wu-involution obstruction; the 2022 version retains it. Debray and Yu's 2024 paper and author-hosted 2025 version give the classical tangent characteristic number and credit older sources. The note supplies a complete topological covering and tangent-microbundle argument covering arbitrary continuous involutions, and a two-row Borel spectral-sequence proof of the odd-primary rank-one upper bound. It claims no new manifold, circle action, classical ingredient or classification.

Circle-cover pullback gives actual free cyclic actions for every odd prime, while nontrivial continuous circle actions are excluded. These do not meet Hanke's abelian fundamental-group hypothesis: their mapping-torus group contains a nontrivial centerless, hence nonabelian, subgroup. metadata.title: A first-order obstruction to Habiro's rank interpolation
metadata.description:
The ordinary integral rank completion printed in Ohtsuki's Conjecture7.30 cannot interpolate the standard unified sl_n invariants of any integral homology sphere with nonzero Casson invariant. A representative in one finite interpolation quotient forces the first q minus1 coefficient to be affine in matrix size n. The classical coefficient formula n(n squared minus1) times the Casson invariant is cubic. For the orientation of the Poincare sphere obtained by minus1 surgery on the left-handed trefoil, sizes1,2,3 give0, minus6, minus24, whose second difference is minus12. This supplies a decisive negative answer to the literal displayed conjecture. It gives no existence criterion at Casson zero and proposes no corrected completion.

metadata.title: A credited finiteness deduction for restricted boundary-twist factorizations
metadata.description: For each fixed genus g ≥ 1, let S(g,1) be an oriented compact surface with one boundary component, and let maps and isotopies fix that boundary pointwise. We prove that ordered positive factorizations of one positive boundary Dehn twist, along non-null-homotopic simple closed curves with repetitions permitted and pairwise geometric intersection at most one, have finitely many simultaneous-conjugacy classes. metadata.title: A type-D4 counterexample to the canonical-potential exponent converse
metadata.description:
The exponent-bound converse stated for canonical GHKK potentials in Schumann's 2021 Oberwolfach report is false. For an explicit reduced word in type D4, the canonical potential has 22 combined monomials, all of coefficient one, and all 22 inequalities define distinct facets, although two monomials have exponent minus two in one canonical coordinate. The chamber-ansatz pullback has all exponents in {-1,0,1}, so the later string-coordinate converse is not refuted. No first-priority or current-openness claim is made.

metadata.title: A fixed-area exceptional set for positive squared-pole sums
metadata.description:

metadata.title: All-load stability of a deterministic-first-chunk file-sharing chain
metadata.description:
We prove positive recurrence for every fixed positive real arrival rate in the four-population deterministic-first-chunk continuous-time Markov chain with a permanent seed, invisible empty waiting rooms, and immediate departure of completed peers. metadata.title: A continuous free product system not generated by its tensor core
metadata.description:
We construct an associative pointed free product system of separable complex Hilbert spaces whose maximal ordered tensor subsystem does not generate the whole free system. Its tensor core is the time-ordered finite-word Fock system, and the closed free hull of that core is the full finite-word Fock system. The ambient system has additional nonzero orthogonal sectors of ordinal words of length below omega squared. A recoverable sigma-finite Gaussian mixture and coordinate-retaining finite-prefix absorption yield countable maximal-run charts and pointed free-product unitaries. The paper proves full associativity and an explicit continuous-field structure including time zero, positive-time local triviality, and continuity of the structural maps and their inverses. A quantitative finite-positive-measure grade-omega witness proves properness for every positive time.

This gives a negative answer in the scalar specialization to the universal tensor-core generation question posed by Michael Skeide in Oberwolfach Reports 6 (2009), 528-530, DOI10.4171/OWR/2009/09. It does not resolve adapted-cocycle, forward tensor-recovery or general classification questions. The stated explicit continuity convention is part of the theorem; arbitrary stronger regularity axioms are not asserted. Classical Fock constructions, standard Gaussian/Radon-Nikodym tools and nonclassical tensor-noise context are credited. The known forward construction from any spatial tensor input has generating tensor core by a direct hull-monotonicity argument, so it cannot itself give this proper-core-hull obstruction.

metadata.title: Tail generation for symmetric free-product states: a general deduction
metadata.description:
For every unital C*-algebra A and every state on its countable universal unital free product invariant under finite permutations, the recursively defined Dykema-Kostler-Williams tail C*-algebra D generates the tail von Neumann algebra T in the original GNS representation: D double commutant equals T. More precisely, the canonical expectation of the represented free-product algebra is weak-operator dense in T, with inputs and outputs bounded by the exact norm of each tail target. No faithful state or representation, separability, trace, factoriality, quantum symmetry or normal extension of the expectation is assumed.

metadata.title: BV generators for polynomial Weyl subalgebras
metadata.description:
For every field k of characteristic zero and every nonzero polynomial h in k[x], the ordinary Hochschild cohomology of A_h = k<x,Y>/(Yx-xY-h(x)), with its canonical cup product and Gerstenhaber bracket, admits a degree-minus-one Batalin-Vilkovisky generator exactly when h is squarefree. The squarefree case has zero bracket and admits Delta=0. If h has a repeated irreducible factor, a central degree-one annihilator forces any bracket generator to vanish on degree one; an explicit cup-zero noncommuting pair then rules out every generator, even without a square-zero requirement. The argument works over the original field without a splitting-field hypothesis. The original embedded h=0 specialization is k[x] and is treated separately.

metadata.title: Logarithmic Bray sampling in symplectic and orthogonal groups
metadata.description:
For every odd prime-power field order q and all sufficiently large natural dimensions n, for every actual fixed strong involution t in Sp(V), O(V), SO(V) or Ω(V), each separately specified t-eigenspace has probability at least c/log n of receiving a strong restriction of the even Bray output inv(tt^g), with g independent and uniformly distributed in the actual group. On a d-dimensional space, strong means both eigenspace dimensions lie in the closed interval [d/3, 2d/3].

The manuscript proves unconditional graph-chart masses for self-adjoint operators, all four orthogonal determinant-character sectors including q=3 and zero-dimensional complements, and an exact half-mass square-spinor refinement. A 192-prescribed-class generation argument using the stated published Burness and Liebeck–Pyber–Shalev results, together with a natural-central-cover and simple-quotient graph argument using 385 disjoint first-success blocks, shows that O(log n·(1+log(1/δ))) independent uniform samples generate a subgroup containing C_G(t)′′ with probability at least 1−δ, for every 0<δ<1.

This addresses the symplectic and orthogonal parts of the fixed-strong-involution Bray sampling problem reported in Oberwolfach Report37/2016, pp2160–2161 (repository problem30003185, PR1330). The linear and unitary marginal/generation results are existing work of Dixon–Praeger–Seress and Glasby–Praeger–Roney-Dougal; their distinguished2-part method and independent diagonal-escape strategy are credited. The 2026 stingray random-power construction has a different target. Bounded priority comparisons do not establish global firstness.

The theorem is asymptotic in natural dimension and concerns sample count at prescribed confidence. It makes no all-dimension, characteristic-two, projective-involution, order-four-lift, similitude or total-running-time assertion, and no claim that a fixed multiplier gives vanishing error. Sp4 zero marginal and arbitrarily large 2:1 non-simultaneous-strength obstructions are explained. The two eigenspace events are separate, not a simultaneous bound.

metadata.title: A free-chain counterexample to a Nash-intersection conjecture
metadata.description:
For the complete family of prime divisors obtained by n successive free point blowups over the smooth complex surface germ, fixing a prefix of k centers with 2 <= k < n gives the closed Nash-set intersection {ord x >= ceil(n/k), ord y >= n}. Five blowups give thresholds (3,5) and (2,5) when two or three centers are fixed. Neither is q(1,j) for any positive integers q,j, so no positive contact multiple of any reference prefix divisor equals the intersection. The proof exhausts all complex free-center choices and treats both charts, satellite limits, identically zero x, constant arcs, exact/at-least contact closures and all integer multiplicities. Explicit separating arcs are nonconstant convergent polynomials.

This is a negative answer to the specified-reference-multiple assertion of Conjecture 1 in Fernandez de Bobadilla, Pe Pereira and Popescu-Pampu, arXiv1501.06898v3 p.31, and Pe Pereira's joint OWR46/2016 contribution p.2679, under every contact/index convention explicitly mapped in the paper. In particular fixing the genuinely free selected c3 still leaves c4,c5 variable. The source uses an intersection; a catalogue union is a transcription discrepancy. Its bare equivalence symbol is undefined and its global indexing inconsistent, so no unique author-intended correction or unspecified replacement is asserted. The intersections ARE maximal divisorial sets for other primitive toric weights; no arbitrary-divisor negative, nonreduced-scheme equality, Conjecture 2 or general Nash-problem solution is claimed.

The standard divisorial/contact and toric framework, and the original paper's combinatorial invariance and cylindrical intersection results, are explicitly credited. The contribution is the complete free-family calculation and reference-ray obstruction.
